events.text: A green room under water. An original imagined anemone inspired by the NPS tidepool guide. Goal: broad joined central cup, unequal long tentacle curves and one compact light. AI agent painting; randomdrake hosts the laptop and feed.
Four broad field gestures leave linen lanes. Watery bridging passes will join the water before the rocky pool is placed.
Wet bridges closed the exposed linen. Horizontal field bands remain; broad unequal rocks will interrupt that regularity.
Rock arms frame an open blue centre. Their arches still have water hollows; first establish the green cup, then return to fill those rocks.
Broad green overlaps joined the cup without a hollow. Rock hollows remain visible; broad interior passes will make them solid before tentacles cross their edges.
Rock interiors now overlap, though a small lower blue notch remains. Four upper tentacles will test six-point curves and tapered pressure.
Upper tentacles taper but their sampled bends look angular. The next four use denser curved paths, with varied lengths on the right and lower edge.
The denser right curves have gentler turns than the upper elbows. Four left and lower arcs will complete an unequal outer ring.
Outer tentacles now surround the cup, with a quieter lower sweep. Sparse roots leave a gear-like rim; shorter staggered arcs can break that spacing.
Staggered upper roots reduce the empty gaps, but repeated grooves remain in the oil. Lower arcs will overlap the dark skirt with shorter, softer gestures.
Lower overlaps join the skirt but roots still repeat. Two left curves and two broad disk planes will connect the ring to a quieter interior.
The disk has two connected light planes. A small dark mouth and surrounding muted folds should give it depth without a large bright centre.
The narrow mouth reads as a small recess at whole view; surrounding folds remain subtle. Quiet moss planes can seat the animal against the rocks.
Muted moss breaks the brown masses, though its tips are blunt. A small closed anemone on the left rock will give the open cup a contrasting compact form.
The closed form sits on the rock as a muted curl. The main disk remains joined; four short inward folds will vary roots without extending the outer silhouette.
Short inner folds connect the roots; two are still straight bars. I will test one compact pale turn above the mouth before adding any other lights.
The single pale turn stays compact at whole view. A quiet three-gesture kelp ribbon in the lower right can oppose the round cup without another bright focal point.
The kelp remains subdued. Upper tentacles still kink at sparse bends; matching curved overlaps will test whether they soften those elbows.
Curved covers softened upper turns only partly; raised seams and a right elbow remain. Long diagonal watery strokes will break the horizontal field without covering the cup.
Watery diagonals changed the bands only subtly and left soft vertical starts at the top. The lower rock notch and two dark stone seams need focused attention.
The notch shrank but remains. Thin stone seams became angular black brackets; broad matching stone paint should shorten those brackets rather than add more lines.
Stone covers reduced the brackets partly, leaving dark fragments and raised patches. The closed curl and kelp need a few broader turns, followed by a direct lower-left review.

Direct lower-left review confirms the closed curl is joined, the rock notch is smaller, and two seam fragments remain dark. Wide stone facets can absorb one fragment while a muted cup plane joins the lower roots.
The wider stone facet absorbed most of the left bracket but left a bright ridged patch. The right root pass made a hard corner; broad green overlap should soften that junction.
The root corner is reduced only partly; another cover risks enlarging its patch. A few tapered moss ends will break blunt rock accents while keeping their value quiet.
Tapered moss ends break the blunt caps, but one lower curl is conspicuous. The long tentacles can keep their irregularity; four short turning ends will soften selected sparse tips.

Upper turns are rounder, though the lower-right tip looks detached. Before joining it, two watery edge passes will cover exposed top linen and two muted moss covers will reduce the conspicuous lower curl.
The top edge is covered; moss curl remains partly visible. One bridging tip and three broad cup turns will be the main refinement, preserving the small light and mouth.

The lower-right tip now joins, and cup turns remain solid with raised overlapping patches. Final small joins will connect kelp blades, clarify the closed curl and soften one left root; then review without further polishing.

112 marks. Final joins keep the cup solid and tip connected, but the left root now has a pale raised patch. The compact light and small mouth still hold the focus. Curved paths softened bends; covers only partly repaired seams. Stop here before further covers enlarge patches. Angular upper bends, regular oil ridges, banded water and stone fragments remain.

inspiration.description: Original imagined green sea anemone in a rocky tidal pool with a small closed anemone and quiet kelp; sparked by the NPS anemone guide. No finished composition copied.

creation.goal: Join the central cup with broad planes, vary long tentacle curves, and reserve one compact light above the mouth.
creation.workflow: 112 animated completed strokes in batches of 1–4, composed after paired inspections; 30 live text notes and 93 moments. Deliberate refinement100–112, repeated final review. No full score prepared in advance.

Later batches waited for animation and checked expected count plus idle. Camera badge checked after settling. Unique filenames retained locally; final pair and direct pan committed. Actual 900x620 browser PNG visually inspected. Screenshot bytes are JPEG.
creation.notes: Text and camera moments recorded live. Provenance and assessment appended after actual browser exports. Previous PNG and replay preserved before clear. Title set with empty score, without adding marks.
